a novel phage-immobilization approach was developed and used to capture hepatitis B core antigen directly from crude Escherichia colihomogenate.

the use of fusion M13 phages as affinity ligands in EBAC can lead to high recovery of core particles with comparable antigenicity to that of particles purified using sucrose gradient ultracentrifugion.

M13 phage immobilized on Streamline base matrix can be used as a ligand in direct capture of HBcAg from E. coli homogeneate and that the introduction of feedstock recycling into EBAC operation can increase the yield of the target product.

the development of an EBAC method for the direct purification of HBcAg from unclarified E. coli feedstock using M13 phage immobilized adsorbent.
the development of a simple and efficient method for the purification of HBcAg from unclarified E. coli feedstock.
the use of phage immobilized expanded bed adsorbents to capture HBc Ag from unclarified E. coli homogeneates.

the fusion phage-immobilization EBAC operation is a promising alternative to sucrose ultracentrifu- gation in the purification of HBcAg.

the use of fusion M13 phages with a disulfide constrained peptide as ligand for expanded bed adsorption (EBA) chromatography has led to a simple, efficient, and rapid purification process for hepatitis B core antigen.
the fusion phage-immobilization strategy has been successfully applied in the purification of HBcAg from unclarified E. coli homogeneates.
